correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the published closed Poincare polynomial. Multiplication by 1-q turns Betti numbers into first differences. Up to the center, double numerator shifts cannot occur, giving an explicit coefficient formula in terms of floor(j/2)+1. Separate odd/even simplifications locate all zero first differences and show positivity before them. Palindromicity gives the decreasing half. Summation yields exactly floor(3n^2/8). The packaged checker independently expands and tests the identities through n=300.

value.rationale: The theorem converts a known generating function for a central moduli space in enumerative geometry into a sharp global description of its cohomological concentration: exact modal height, exact plateau width and location, and strict unimodality off the plateau for every target dimension. This is a natural family-level topological invariant useful for comparing stable-map spaces across dimension, rather than an arbitrary coefficient extraction.
